name: Longer Ray7 7.5W
tagline: The entry Ray7: a fine 7.5W diode on a 405 × 410 mm open frame for detailed engraving under $250
tldr: The Ray7 7.5W is the cheapest version of Longer's new open-frame engraver: $229.99 on Longer's store in October 2026. It keeps the Ray7 frame, 600 mm/s motion, Wi-Fi and 405 × 410 mm bed, with the finest spot of the range at 0.06 × 0.06 mm. It is an engraver first: cutting stops at thin wood, card and felt, and takes several passes.
mainObjective: Detailed engraving on wood, leather and slate on a full-size bed at the lowest price

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cannot: Plywood thicker than ~3 mm in practice

pros: Finest beam of the Ray7 range at 0.06 × 0.06 mm according to Longer, well suited to photos and small text
$229.99 for a 405 × 410 mm bed with Wi-Fi and 600 mm/s motion (Longer store, October 2026)
Low-power module is easier to tune on leather, paper and card without burning through
cons: Cutting is limited to thin material: about 2–3 mm basswood per pass by our estimate
Photo fills take roughly 24–36 min for 10 × 10 cm by our estimate, the slowest of the range
Air pump, autofocus and camera are all extras on top of the $229.99 price
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 7.5W version of the Longer Ray7. Take it if you mostly engrave gifts, signs and photos and rarely cut. Compare the other Ray7 versions with the chips above if cutting plywood matters: the frame, bed and software stay the same, only the laser module changes. It is a new machine with no independent reviews yet.
proTips: Work at high power and moderate speed for dark, even photo engraving, and save cutting for paper, card, felt and 2–3 mm basswood in two passes. Use the 50 mm focal distance carefully: without the optional autofocus, refocus each time the material thickness changes.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 7.5W Ray7 brings Longer's new frame, Wi-Fi and 600 mm/s motion to a budget price, and its 0.06 × 0.06 mm spot is the sharpest in the range for portraits, fine lettering and small logos.
editorialDepth.limitations: It is not a cutter: anything beyond thin basswood, card and felt needs many passes. Open frame: wear safety glasses and extract the smoke. The Ray7 is new, so long-term reliability is not yet documented by independent reviews.

faq.question: What can the Ray7 7.5W cut?
faq.answer: Longer does not publish cutting figures for this version. By our estimate it cuts paper, card, felt, thin leather and about 2–3 mm basswood per pass; 3 mm plywood takes two passes or more. Treat it as an engraver with occasional light cuts.

faq.question: Ray7 7.5W or Ray7 15W?
faq.answer: The 15W costs $299.99 against $229.99 for the 7.5W (Longer store, October 2026). For $70 more it roughly doubles cutting capacity and speeds up fills; keep the 7.5W only if you engrave almost exclusively and value the finest spot.

faq.question: Is the Ray7 7.5W a good first laser?
faq.answer: Yes for engraving on a budget: belts come pre-installed, it connects over Wi-Fi and works with Longer Studio or LightBurn. As an open-frame laser it needs safety glasses, ventilation and a fire-safe surface.
